utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Mr. Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-02-60-T, the Prosecutor versus Vidoje Blagojevic and Dragan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning, everybody, and good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Did you have a good rest last night?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are you ready to start?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Today it won't be long. Yes, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Stojanovic: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With your permission, we will go today through these documents containing references to your name, and this may be related to your overall testimony. Thus, I believe, we would go through and finish before the end of this session. If you remember, we began discussing yesterday the intercepts or, as they called them, tactical intercepts from Dekici.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With the usher's assistance, I would like to show the witness B/C/S copies of the exhibit we used yesterday. It's the Prosecution Exhibit P121, and we identified it as D110/3.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vukotic, if I may draw your attention to the part of intercepts dating back to the 14th of July - that's on page 2 - for identification and for the record it's ERN 00848950. If you will please look at the middle of the page, time mark 19.30 hours. At that time a conversation was intercepted between "Omega 2" and "Vuk," unknown collocutors. Note of the ABiH operator says: "Our men tore their right flank. They said in code that our men are firing from elevation 207." Can you tell us, please: Did you have this conversation around 1930 on that day?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember this exchange in particular, but I know that in the radio network the call sign of "Omega" was used by public security forces, that is, the police. I believe "Omega 2" was at the time deputy chief of police, Mane Djuric.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that day, on the 14th of July in the evening, did you have a radio link with Mane Djuric or "Omega 2", his code-name?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say that I had any sort of coordination with police units except for what I told you yesterday. In Kula town, Kula Grad, where police forces had arrived, at that time I tried to brief them as to the whereabouts of the units of the VRS and in the sense of escorting the column or monitoring the column, as I explained yesterday. I don't remember this specific conversation, but I'm certain, however, that the call sign of "Omega" was used by police units to be precise. I had no advisory role with the police, nor did I issue any orders. I was just one of the soldiers up there who was linking up these forces in the field.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just one clarification to remove any doubt: In one of the exhibits, we saw that on the 14th of July in the evening executions were already taking place in the area of Orahovac. That's why I wish to ask you once again: Where are you at the time of this conversation?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At Kula Grad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For identification, Your Honour, this is page ERN 00848951.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And for you, Mr. Vukotic, this is the lower half of the page in the B/C/S copy. This is an intercept between "Igman 1" and "Lovac 1". The conversation goes as follows: "Pass Vuk on to me. Give me hill. Can you hear me? I will send Aco." Vuk replies, or maybe somebody else: "Aco should get ready to go left of you. I am at the largest hill. Send a unit to the long-haired blond one." According to the indictment, this is the time when Dragan Jokic is the duty officer in the Zvornik Brigade, and the long-haired blond one is identified as the duty officer. Can you answer this?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This reflects the beginning of combat operations in the area of Maricici, Snagovo, Velja Glava, and on the axes and in areas we discussed yesterday. "Igman 1", as far as I remember, is properly identified here as my signalsman, who was attached to me, as I said yesterday, together with his RUP field radio. So "Igman" is a part of this mixed artillery division. I don't remember the name of the soldier, but he was operating the RUP radio. Aco, referred to here, is obviously Aleksandar Kostic. I told you that he was commander of the provisional scouts group which had the first clash with ABiH forces in the area of Velja Glava on the 13th. And if you remember yesterday, I told you that I asked the Chief of Staff to pull out this group. My request was approved. And as requested, this group was then sent to another area, the area of Snagovo and Maricici, where fire was much more intense by this time. This reference to Brdo means my clerk for intelligence, my intelligence officer. He was part of one group that was between Velja Glava and Snagovo. This is how I interpret, how I read this part of the text, if I can be at all correct in view of the time that has passed since.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Just let me clarify why I ask this question. It says here: "Send a unit to the blond-haired -- to the long-haired blond man (Djoko) ST.duty officer." Does this have anything to do with Dragan Jokic, then-duty officer of the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which Djoko is meant here, and I cannot answer either yes or no to your question because this text begs the question whether only our tactical conversations were being intercepted at the time or the ABiH eavesdropping group was also listening to the conversations between the radio centre of the brigade and other participants in the network. It's very difficult to say anything conclusively. I can only surmise that this is a reference to the duty officer at the radio centre but I'm telling you this is only my assumption.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does this mean anything to you: "Send a unit to the long-haired blond man"?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to move on to the next page, ERN number 00848952. It's again, the 14th of July, 1995. We see an exchange that reads as follows: "Igman 1: Vuk has left to tour, to inspect the line. If you need anything, find him through Premijer." Tell us again: Who is "Igman 1" and who is informing who in this sentence about your movements?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before I answer your question, I would like to go back to this part that you read. If you look carefully at the transcript, you will see clearly that if Djoko's group is going to the left of Maric - and we are talking about Milan Maric, who is also in the same area where there is fighting with the column - then it is more than obvious that the entire conversation is focussing on the area of combat and confrontation with the column that we spent the entire day of yesterday discussing. And now, in answer to your question. As I emphasised, "Igman 1" is obviously the call sign for the signalsman operating the RUP device, which was my parallel communication with the Chief of Staff. And if you will allow me -- Could you say again what are you focussing on in this question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, "Igman 1", as far as I understand, is the radio accompanying you. "Igman 1" is telling somebody, "Vuk has gone to inspect the line. If you need anything, find him through Premijer." Whom is "Igman 1" informing on your movements?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is maintaining communication between me and the chief of Staff, since he is speaking in the first person singular, which he would not allow himself to do speaking to a chief of staff, he must be talking to a signalsman in the other unit. And as to the substances, this must refer to the time when I had gone towards Mladjevac or Maritice on one of my regular tours to see the extent to which the units were linked up in the course of combat operations that we've discussed. And if I may add to explain this situation more clearly: He says "If you need anything, find him through Premijer." Since I have a hand-held short-wave radio on me at the time, and if you are climbing down this slope - the terrain is very uneven - it's not always possible to maintain communication through the radio network, and at such moments Premijer helps out and transmits information from one to another.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "in simplex," and that's a word which we've had the opportunity to see in the intelligence report of the 12th of July, what do you mean by that? Could you please help us. We don't know these terms.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a short-wave radio conversation involving a direct link. There's no intermediary. You are directly connected to the other participant. If this is not the case, then somebody needs to mediate, even though communications people know this, there is a simplex communication, a direct communication, and a duplex communication. A duplex communication implies that you -- or that both participants can speak at the same time and listen to one another. This is usually a telephone connection. That would be a duplex connection. A simplex connection would mean that one person is speaking and the other can only listen, and that is why in radio traffic you have the following terms. When you hear something, you can say "Roger" and then "over" at the beginning and at the end of the conversation, your part or the other person's part.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. On the same page - we are continuing - we are still on the 14th of July. 18.25 is the last time that is written in. There's a conversation between "Lovac 1" and "Igman 1". In brackets it says "Vuk." The conversation states: "They have captured a MUP commander who was securing the flank. There is a mass of people in front of me. We need to close the road that you and I passed the other night. They will go this way for sure." Could you please tell us who is participating in this conversation? Do you personally remember that conversation and what is it about?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not very clear to me except for the part about which commander from MUP it is. It is Zoran Jovanovic, who is from the military police, and we discussed this yesterday. It is not quite clear here who is calling whom; did "Lovac 1" call or "Igman 1". The way it is here, it seems that the communications officer who's standing next to the Chief of Staff, is speaking to the communications person who was with me at Kula Grad to maintain this parallel link. I assume that this refers to the report about how the units had already arrived at this Snagovo- Zvornik road, and I assume that the conversation is between two soldiers who are both or were both most probably a part of the forces between the 12th and the 13th. And if you recall, that's the same component of the force where I was with the Chief of Staff, with the tank, the self-propelled gun and the Praga. And that is why they mention this, the road where we passed the other night. That's where they will pass for sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question about the 14th of July is as follows: Did you at any point have any radio communications with the duty officer in Dragan Jokic's brigade?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I would now like to move to the 15th of July. On the 15th of July - this is ERN number 00848953 -

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: 954.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There is an intercepted conversation on that day. It's on the middle of the page for the 15th of July. Could you please find it, Mr. Vukotic. I would like to thank the usher. There is no need for her to remain standing. We can follow it from here and then when we need you, we will ask you to help us again. It states here: "Vuk ordered for Aco to go with his people to see Golub and he will deploy them further. On the right side in front of us the white belts should go." In parentheses it says: "VPA." I assume that means military police. Can you remember when this conversation took place? Because it states at the bottom the time of another conversation, 8.05 hours. Could you please tell us what this is about.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not be serious enough if I could say that I could remember every single conversation or a part thereof. I don't remember everything that was happening on the ground. But from these intercepts and generally from these pages of the transcript that I have in front of me, I can just recall the overall situation where there was fire throughout the entire region. There was firing all over the place. So this is about transferring certain groups and units and so on, because at the time we were in a war zone where, in the depth of it, in the immediate depth of it, close to our lines, we had conflicts with forces of the 28th Division and our units. This is a typical movement of units to certain firing positions. I recall that the call sign throughout the entire combat operations of Golub was the call sign of the mortar platoon from the Podrinje Special Forces Unit. This also then confirms what I said yesterday, that the unit that I saw from Kula returned and deployed in the brigade sector. This group of military police that is going towards Golub logically should secure the positions of the mortar platoon, because generally the mortar platoon and in practice always has to be secured, especially because combat operations are already there. It's very difficult to have a complete overview of the situation because many infiltrated groups or groups that are straggling are there. There is no classic line of defence any more or a classic frontal -- front of attack any more. We need to keep in mind that the soldiers of the B and H army and the soldiers of the Zvornik Brigade are already intermingled in that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if you allow me, on the 15th in the morning at 8.05 hours - same ERN page - there is a note. It's a conversation between Vuk and "Lovac 1". "We have two of their men captured. A number of people from -- Glodjani remained in Glodi." So this is what was said in the morning. Could you please tell us who is speaking and what this is about.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Glodi is far from the place we're talking about now. Glodi are in the area of Kamenica. The area where I was is at least 10 to 12 kilometres away. Glodi is a settlement through which the column passed. I will remind you that this was the sector of Kamenica. There is something illogical here, that I would be informing "Lovac 1" from Kula. That is not quite clear to me here, what this is about. On the other hand, I must say, and you must keep in mind, if you are analysing the overall situation clearly that, at the time members of the Milici unit, the Vlasenica unit, and so on are also carrying out certain operations throughout this entire region, so that I am not sure what this is exactly about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in this time period, were you aware that in this intermingling of units some members of the B and H army were captured?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This happened for sure, because I told you that on this whole terrain there were different groups and people were captured. I specifically - and this was logical - they never reached Kula. They never reached the sector where I was, because had they reached Kula, it would all have been over. That would have meant the end for Kula. They did not get to that point. So from that position, I know that there were no prisoners.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us move to page 008956 [as interpreted]. This is the 15th of July. It's 9.35 in the morning. It's a conversation between "Lovac 1" and Vuk, which says: "Include the forces to the left and to the right in the operations. I saw them. They want to block the road through Krizevici towards Planinci. Afterwards, they were directing the artillery. Let Zoka block the road towards Planinci." This is in the morning on the 15th of July. Who is participating in this conversation and where are these participants, "Lovac 1" and "Vuk"?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm still at my position, and "Lovac 1" is obviously the Chief of Staff or his communications officer who, of course, is conveying the information and certain orders on his behalf. It is evident that the forces of the 28th Division were already very close to Baljkovica, because the next village beyond Krizevici is Baljkovica. Just as Planinci are right next to the Karakaj-Crni Vrh-Caparde-Sekovici road, since they're on this parallel communication, the Igman 1 communications officer with the RUP-12 had communication with the mixed artillery division, which did not have a short-wave communication with us. So it's most probable that the Chief of Staff, not having a direct communication at that point because he was at some place where he could not directly convey orders through the RUP-12 to the mixed artillery division. So he was conveying them via this communications officer, who is part of the mixed artillery division and that is why it states here "they were directing the artillery later." So this is a request for barrage fire. This is a request for artillery barrage fire in order to block the forces from cutting the road and coming around the back of the units of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. For the transcript, if we can just repeat once again: "Lovac 1" is Obrenovic.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It should be Obrenovic, as far as I can recall. I'm afraid that in the analysis of the previous two pages, I'm afraid that I perhaps at one point mixed up "Igman 1" and "Lovac 1". There is the possibility of that, but now there doesn't seem to be any point in going back to that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It says: "At 9.35 here on the 15th of July, Lovac 1." So Obrenovic says: "I saw them. They are trying to block the road through Krizevici, towards Planinci. Could you please tell us approximately the area from where he can see the road through Krizevici towards Planinci. Where was he at that point so that he was able to see that? If you can recall that.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be irresponsible on my part to determine where anyone was who was not in my direct line of sight. The road to Krizevici towards Planinci can be seen through the area of Kitovnice - I am sure of that - and it could be seen from several points or positions, for example, from Kitovnice; I don't know whether from that elevation, which is right above Baljkovica, I don't know whether it's possible to see it from there. Of course you can see it from that inner sector, and also you can see it from the sector of Orahovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Orahovac is a settlement which is in front of Snagovo on the Zvornik-Kalesija road.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. If you are following the road, the regional road Zvornik-Karakaj, then Orahovac, then the road forks off to the right for Kitovnice then goes on ahead towards Planinci, Crni Vrh, and Caparde. So already after Orahovac the next village, which is between Orahovac and Kitovnice, is the village of Krizevici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And if this will assist, we will finish with this. Let's just look at this -- the continuation of this conversation so that we can perhaps confirm what you are stating. So it's on the same page. It's conversation L -- between L and L1: "Right of the road to capture that area," and then L continues, "Do not send the people over -- through Krizevici, send them through Jardani and Kitovnice." Does this show, possibly, where "Lovac 1" was at the time? We're speaking about Obrenovic. We're talking about the conversation L-L1. It says: "To capture the area right of the road." And then I'm continuing, because this is not translated into B/C/S: "Send the forces -- a force of 40 people." This is what L1 says: "Do not send groups through Krizevici. Go over Jardani and Kitovnice." Where do you think "Lovac 1" was at the time, Obrenovic? If you can help us and if that can confirm your hypothesis, I would be satisfied.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm really sorry, but I cannot determine the position of any participant who was not in my line of sight. I don't know how much I helped you by telling you from which positions that area could be seen and by providing you the geographical points. I am drawing this conclusion. It's clear from a military standpoint that subordinated units that are arriving to this sector of combat operations should be told to go in the direction of Jardani-Kitovnice because then they would avoid a large section of the road towards Crni Vrh. And in this area, where these major battles are already waging, Orahovac, Krizevici, Batkovic and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was exactly what I was about to ask you. In this way, they would avoid passing through Orahovac; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We have had a lot of testimony here to the effect that on the 15th of July precisely at this time there were burials going on in the Orahovac area. At that point, did you know anything about this?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In this exhibit, Your Honours, there are six or seven other intercepts mentioning the name of Vuk. But because time is of the essence, this is after the 15th when Dragan Jokic was no longer the duty operations officer, so I will not go into this. There may be questions about it later on, but please don't hold it against me for not cross-examining on it. I will now ask the witness to briefly go through Prosecutor's Exhibit P507, that is, D93/3 for purposes of identification, and this is the duty operations officer's logbook. I will show the witness these documents one by one. Your Honours, this is the logbook of the duty operations officer, and we will go through the notes very briefly just for purposes of identification. I will use an excerpt, ERN number 03089337. This is the entry for the 13th of July, 1995, and in one place it says -- in the B/C/S version, it's 09 -- 02934579. Vukotic and Petkovic through the radio centre call Obrenovic "At the place where you were last night and come up there." [As interpreted]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you recall what the duty officer is recording here?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably this is the request or the order by the Chief of Staff to go back to the place where we had spend the night between the 12th and the 13th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does this mean that Petkovic was to go with you?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall, but it's possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the same page for the same day, the duty operations officer noted the following: "Vukotic needs to call Aco and Aco needs to be dispatched to Dzafin Kamen to the 4th Battalion or that Aco needs to be dispatched to the 4th Battalion."

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What date is this?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The 13th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall this in any detail, but Aco was at Dzafin Kamen, so yes, he was sent there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I will now go on to the next page. For identification, this is ERN number 03089338. In B/C/S, it's 02935743. These are also notes by the duty officer of the 13th of July. At the top of the page, it says the following: "Premijer called and asked that Vukotic calls 365." Can you help us and try to explain what this note is about.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have already told you that Premijer, apart from having communication with his commander of the Podrinje Detachment of the special forces, could at the same time have communications with me but also communications by telephone with the duty operations officer. When he was unable to pass on information either to his commander or the necessary intelligence to me, he could pass on this information by telephone to the duty operations officer, especially if he couldn't find me or the Chief of Staff and in those cases he would ask the duty officer to mediate. He would ask him to try and find us on the field and tell us to contact him. I think this is the context in which this note was made.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I would now like to show you the next page on which your name is mentioned. This is, for the record, ERN in English 03089342, and in B/C/S the ERN number is 02935747. Mr. Vukotic, this is dated the 14th of July, 1995, when the duty operations officer was Dragan Jokic. At the bottom of the page it says: "At 1300 hours, situation normal. Palma 2." Then it says: "Vukotic and Aco to be at full combat readiness at 1500 hours." Can you see this? This is the last note on this page.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you please repeat what date this was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The 14th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It says: "At 1300 hours, situation normal. Palma 2." Then it says: "Vukotic and Aco to be on the full combat equipment."

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who "Palma 2" is. I don't know why it says "Vukotic." Vukotic never went to see the duty operations officer and he never issued orders as to who was to be ready and why and so on. So I'm not quite sure what this is about. If I recall rightly, between the 13th and the 14th Aco was at Dzafin Kamen. I said yesterday that in the evening of the 13th he was pulled back from Dzafin Kamen and sent from there; whether to the area where there were combat operations, I can't recall, but I really don't know why. It's possible that there was a request by me for Aco's group to be sent. It's possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. The next example --

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to stress that Aco Kostic, with his group of policemen throughout these combat operations was involved in combat with this column, so it's possible that I requested that he be ready.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This may be a good opportunity to ask you the following: What was the duty of the duty operations officer? Did he only note this down without entering into the essence of the content of all this, or did he participate in it all?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the brigade commander or the Chief of Staff was there, the duty officer -- without wishing to derogate his duty, was simply a courier and a switchboard operator. His duty was to find the quickest way of passing information on to the Chief of Staff or the brigade commander, and that was the end of his function. I don't know how clear I have been, but based on my experience - not as a duty officer, because I was never that - but I was able to see that his role was what I have just described, for the most part.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Vukotic. I will take an example of an officer from your organ. In the notes made by the duty officer on a day when Dragan Jokic was on duty, the 14th of July, there is a note as follows: "Salapura called that Beara and Drago should report to Gulic." What I would like to know is the following: I assume you know who Salapura is. Was the duty officer supposed to know why Drago and Beara should report to Golic and did he have the right to ask Salapura, "Why are you asking for this?"

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The answer to this is quite clear. He didn't need to know and he didn't need to ask.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us go back to the 15th of July. ERN number in English, 03089354; in B/C/S, 02935759. Mr. Vukotic, this refers to the 15th of July, 1995, and the duty operations officer, I think, was no longer Dragan Jokic. He wrote a note: "Obrenovic should urgently report to Vuk." Can you comment on this? What is this about?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was probably having a lot of problems in the field because you said this was on the 15th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only on that day, but for many days afterwards there were a lot of problems in that area through which the column was passing and where combat operations were going on. I was probably having problems in the woods, and I was asking for the Chief of Staff to contact me because I suppose I had important information to pass on to him and I needed to ask for his help, ask him what I should do further up there. I am sure that was the context. I'm sure I needed something.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this duty officer supposed to know or did he have to know why you needed to contact Obrenovic, or was it sufficient for you to say through your communications line, "Pass on the message that Obrenovic should contact me urgently"?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I did not have any communication line with the duty operations officer. I probably tasked one of my communications men to look for the Chief of Staff, because communication between the two of us had been cut off. It's very hard to recall all this now after such a long time, but this was conditionally speaking simply mediating, passing on a message, linking up two commanding officers, and that was all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Vukotic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we have three dates in the duty officer's logbook, the 16th, 17th, 19th, and by your leave I will not go into this, in view of the time, because Dragan Jokic was no longer the operations officer. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Vukotic.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will now ask the usher to assist us and hand the witness D129/3, which is a statement by Nedzad Ahmetovic which he gave to the OTP on the 28th of September, 2001.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vukotic, at one point you said that you had an opportunity of interrogating this witness.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We have before us the statement given by Nedzad Ahmetovic on the 28th of September, 2001 to the investigators of the Office of the Prosecutor. At one point he says the following - and this is on page 4 in B/C/S - the last paragraph on page 4 in B/C/S, he says that on the 15th of July he was interrogated by a VRS officer. "This was done on the second floor of the premises. The officer told me that they had searched my house in Srebrenica and that they had found a diary. This officer asked me if it was my diary. And I said no, it probably belonged to Adil Hasanovic, who was a refugee who was staying in my house. This officer showed me another diary, asking if it belonged to Naser Oric. I replied that if the writing is nice, it did not belong to Naser Oric but probably to Ramiz Becirevic." I wanted to ask you: In the words of this witness in this statement, is the reference to a VRS officer who interrogated him in fact a reference to you? And what happened to this person whom you interrogated?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to emphasise before this Trial Chamber, because I believe it is important to say before replying to your question, in view of one's personal participation in the war in Bosnia and Herzegovina, everyone including me took a long, hard look at what happened. As for what happened to this man, I was very happy to learn that this man was alive when I talked to the investigators when giving my statement. The person who spoke to Nedzad was indeed me; however, the things as reflected here are not quite correct, although I don't believe there was any ill-intent on the part of Nedzad Ahmetovic. To be precise, Nedzad Ahmetovic is one of the soldiers from the column we discussed. Marko Dzajic, a member of the Podrinje detachment of the Special Forces, found him on the road from Drinjaca to Zvornik. So he was separated from the column. And directly from the gate, he was the only -- the only prisoner who came directly from the gate to my offices, and I don't think you can see that from this statement. Dzajic called me from the gate and said that he had in his hands a very interesting soldier, because on the way to the barracks he realised that this man knew a lot. He was very frightened and exhausted, and he told the soldier already on the way back that he was the signalsman of Naser Oric and that's why Dzajic called me to take him over, and I did speak to him. I did interview him. I did inform the intelligence section of the Drina Corps about the substance of this interview, and I was indeed one of the commanding officers who suggested that this soldier was able to contribute very significantly to preventing combat around Zepa, because Zepa was also a subject of interest to the VRS and that's why it was taken over by the intelligence administration. As far as I know, although I was never in that area in myself, all casualties were indeed prevented in the area of Zepa. And as far as Nedzad is concerned, I am prepared to confront him at any time, because I believe I was never violent at any point. I treated him decently. I think I was one of the officers who gave him food and drink and treated him fairly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He indeed says that in his statement. He says: "After the interrogation was over, the treatment changed. They moved me to another building," et cetera. But are you saying that combat was avoided around Zepa among other things because Nedzad was able through communications equipment to establish contact between the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina and the Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's exactly what I'm saying, because this young man maintained the so-called package radio communication with the command of the Tuzla Corps and even the Main Staff of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In one place, he says that happened on the 15th of July. Does that coincide with your recollection?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so. I think it could have been later, maybe the 16th; however, I'm not saying that the 15th could not be correct at all because I think I descended from Kula for the first time on the 15th. However, I'm not sure about the date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Maybe another exhibit will help clarify this and refresh your memory.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With the usher's assistance, let me show you - and then we will be through with these exhibits - the exhibit that we identified as D130/3. The source belongs to the Prosecution, and it is in fact an intelligence report sent by the intelligence organ of the Zvornik Brigade on the 18th of July, 1995 to the Drina Corps Command -- or rather, its intelligence department, intelligence section.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this report, Mr. Vukotic - shall we look at it together - could you tell me what is the date on the document?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 18th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To whom is it sent?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The intelligence section of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who is the author?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Judging by the style, it's me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it your name underneath, signed?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see a bit of my handwriting on this. At first I wasn't sure, because I only saw the printed text, but now I see the handwriting as well. The handwriting is mine and the signature is mine, so it's an authentic document created by me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In a part of this report, we can read: "Live speech. Nedzad Ahmetovic, son of Avdo and Mula, computer operator, maintaining the digital communications systems in the headquarters of the 28th administration of the VRS General Staff, says that Ajub Golic and a mountain battalion stayed to secure the end of the column and that his battalion," et cetera. So it says "Live source. Nedzad Ahmetovic." Is this the same person who gave that statement we discussed previously?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could this document refresh your memory as to your contact with Nedzad Ahmetovic in view of the date of this report, the 18th of July?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I would have waited from the 15th to the 18th to send this report. Let me just see at what time this was transmitted. I cannot read the stamp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It says: "21.08 hours" on the stamp.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's precisely why I'm saying that this contact could have been on the 17th; however, it also says that the source had already been handed over to the intelligence administration, so it could have been on the 15th as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In conclusion, Mr. Vukotic, how long did you stay in the army as a professional?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until 1998, May 1998.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that, you took up another job.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I transferred to the police administration and worked there for two years. In the year 2000, I said my final farewell to all kinds of uniforms and took up a job that essentially corresponded to my original training: I went into politics.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What are you doing now, Mr. Vukotic?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am the People's Deputy in the Assembly of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For which party?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Democratic Party.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And to finish with this line of questioning: In the post-war period and after everything that happened in the course of the investigation about Srebrenica and all the knowledge that it yielded, did you at any time, as a politically active person, as a native of Zvornik, have you ever heard anything about the involvement of Dragan Jokic in all that?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Vukotic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, these were all my questions. Thank you for bearing with me in my first examination of a witness. Mr. Vukotic, you will now be answering questions by Mr. Karnavas and perhaps Mr. Waespi, the Prosecutor. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stojanovic. I think there's some problems with the using of the documents. Since this is your first witness and since you are doing the direct examination, I think we should follow the practice as we did in the direct examination of the Prosecution's case as well as in Mr. Karnavas's case; that is, you have to furnish the list of exhibits to be shown to the witness beforehand and indicating whether those documents have been admitted or not. If the document has been admitted into the evidence, you don't have to furnish -- to have them copied and furnished to the other party and to the Bench. If they are not, you have to supply with us those documents all together before the direct examination, rather than, you know, giving us one piece of a document whenever you are using it. We are a little bit confused, you know, with all those documents at this moment. But anyway, this is the first witness, and you have a lot of opportunities to improve this practice.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. We will certainly do that, although I have to say I believe we supplied all these exhibits in a timely manner, both to the Prosecution and to the Trial Chamber, including the list of exhibits we are going to use. But if any misunderstanding remains, we will take care to remove it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: It's time for a break, and we'll take a break and we'll resume at quarter to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Karnavas, do you have any questions to put to this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I just have a couple of questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If we could go into private session. Private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, we'll go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Waespi, your cross-examination, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, I think we can stay in private session for a while. I think we still are; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We will -- we'll go back to the private session, please. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And if we can flip further to the page 27 in the English version, which could be put onto the ELMO. And in the B/C/S version, it's just about three pages later, ERN number 02935764. And it's again the second paragraph, and it's the 16th July now. And I'll read the passage and we see it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "At 1000 hours. Security centre asking Vukotic to call them urgently regarding a captured Muslim." Can you tell us more about that?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I need to stress once again that I really do not recall any details. I'm not ruling out the possibility. I'm not ruling out the possibility that I perhaps took part in such a conversation, but I also assume that I have no recollection of such a moment because this is quite unusual because of our relations. I did not have any case with the security organ in our brigade, including this one. I say again: I'm not ruling out the possibility that I did take part in such a conversation, but I don't recall anything of substance about it, so I cannot claim with certainty yes or no. When we're talking about cooperation between the security organs, it states in the military rules that the intelligence organ -- the intelligence organ -- in order to gather information and in order to secure from an intelligence aspect combat operations can exchange information with the civilian security structures. But this was not my practice because usually the organ of military security and the organ of civilian -- the military security organ and the civilian security organ had something that was called counter-intelligence activities and activities in the depth as well as work on their territory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With your leave, Your Honour, I'm afraid we have a problem with interpretation. During those days in Zvornik there was a police security centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but we don't want the witness testifying here -- I mean, the lawyer testifying to clear up issues related to what this person is saying. These are issues at -- that are part of the contested matter. This isn't just something, a map reference or something, and so I don't believe it's appropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Well, Mr. Stojanovic, I think this is exactly the question the Prosecution put to the witness. Let the witness tell us about it. Okay? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I had no other intention than to clear up interpreting issues in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I understand about that, yes. You may proceed, Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you told us yesterday that you were in Kula Grad, south of Zvornik, this elevated point from, I believe, the 13th --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: At this point I'm going to object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I thought he was going to clarify the point, Your Honour, regarding the security centre. He asked the question earlier on: Does he know anything about the security centre. And the gentleman said which one. And then Mr. Stojanovic intervened and said he wanted to clarify it. And then Mr. McCloskey popped up and said there was no need, that we should get it from the witness. I think before we move on the gentleman should be given an opportunity to explain which security centre -- if he knows -- this notebook is referring to. That's all. I think because it may -- there is a civilian versus a military and I think that that needs clarification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, if you look back at the answer of this witness, the witness said that he did not remember that at all, and then he explained that there was two branches: One is military security office; the other is the civilian one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I totally agree with you, Your Honour. But the question then should have been posed: In this particular notebook, do you know which of the two are being referenced to?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: If the witness did not remember this conversation or this call, are you going to ask the witness to speculate which one?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No. I would rather have the witness say, "I cannot say one way or the other."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I don't mind, you know, if --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: -- if Mr. Waespi could, you know, ask a question, you know, about that. But actually, you know -- Yes, Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, I'd like to move on to Kula Grad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe you told us that you were in Kula Grad from the 13th July onwards. I believe 16th or 17th July, that's when you came back.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember the exact date when I came back, but I know that is where I spent most of my time in this period. I know that I left for Kula Grad on the 13th, but I don't know the exact date when I came back. But since every word said here is important, and I have no taboo topics here, I want to clarify once again. There is a public security centre in Zvornik. In fact, there was a public security centre in Zvornik at the time. Within the frame work of that centre, there is only one unit in the same building, which is the basis of the national security centre. Plus, there is a national security unit and an intelligence unit in the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. But you don't know which one was meant, looking at this brief reference out of the logbook I showed to you.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose this is a reference to this national security section, but it doesn't impose any obligation on me either to report or not to report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Because you don't recall the reference. You can't really know what the reference is about; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I cannot recall. I really cannot recall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, before we go on, just a point of clarification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Because the record now would have us believe that it happened but he just doesn't recall it. That's what I'm afraid, that we're playing with semantics. It's not a matter whether he recalls. Because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, no matter what kind of terminology used, the idea is very clear, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well. I just don't want him in closing arguments saying -- he just doesn't recall. It doesn't mean it didn't happen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we don't know whether it happened or not. We -- actually, we don't know what is -- whether it's happened or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may proceed, Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thanks, Mr. President. Perhaps it's safer we return the document; otherwise, we are coming back to that all the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You had, I believe you testified yesterday, a very good view from Kula Grad; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you also told us that you've seen units returning back to the area of responsibility of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you also see in the evening and night of the 13th July hundreds of Muslim prisoners being shipped towards Zvornik? Did you see that?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on the 14th July, in the morning, perhaps late morning, there was a huge column; buses, trucks, a white APC in front, perhaps even a blue Golf. A huge column going the very road you observed the returning troops. Have you seen this huge column on the 14th of July?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I have to stress that from Kula Grad there is very good visibility for the part of the road from Divic to the entrance into Zvornik. You can see clearly 3 to 4 hundred metres of that road, and from Kula Grad you can see a vehicle. You can't see who's in the vehicle. But the point is I wasn't looking there. I wasn't looking to that side, unless I was expecting my units, because due to the overall situation developing in the field and the requirement for units to come back urgently, it is only logical that I was keen to see on that road vehicles carrying our units on their way back to the brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you just told us you could look into the vehicles. So this --

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But you can distinguish a military vehicle from a civilian one. So when I was looking for our units, I could clearly see military trucks and military vehicles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you are telling us you, the Chief of Intelligence, the most senior intelligence man in the Zvornik area, you would have missed a huge column of trucks and buses, even a UN APC. You would have missed that on the 4th -- on the 14th of July, 1995? Are you telling that to the Court?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It may sound illogical in view of my job that I was performing at the headquarters of the brigade, but I cannot tell you that I saw something that I didn't see. I wasn't observing the road all the time. The events that I have recounted took place exactly on the opposite side of that road. From Kula Grad you have a panoramic view, because it is a high point. You have a panoramic view of that section of the road. However, the focus of my attention was on the column attempting to break through and the events taking place in front of the defence lines of the Zvornik Brigade involving the 2nd Corps of the BH army. Of course I heard much later from other people that using the asphalt main road, a huge column of buses passed that could be seen from Mali Zvornik, from the Serbian side, and -- of course I heard all that, just as every other citizen of Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, just let me ask you: These other buses you mentioned, the huge column of buses. When was that?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the one I heard about?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you I didn't see any buses. Only at one point on the 14th in the afternoon when that unit came back, I was very keen to meet that unit and I noticed them, but I saw no other vehicles or buses. I know about the rest only from the stories I heard four or five days later, stories that had to do with how idiotic it was for somebody to try to cover all this up when the column was so huge. I heard all about that much later, just as you did, and of course I was horrified.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I wasn't the Chief of Intelligence at that time, so there is a difference between the two of us. Let me go back to the document you were shown this morning, the 18th July 1995 document. It's Exhibit Number D130/3. And you told us that you were aware of this document. You even recognised your handwriting. Now, let me just read out the first line, paragraph of this report, which is dated 18th of July, 1995, your intelligence report to the Drina Corps: "Since the last report, which has been confirmed by events described in combat reports (since the dynamics of the events required us to remain in the field), the information collected is as follows..." Now, obviously you are aware of the combat reports which have been filed from the brigade to the corps; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not necessarily. Not necessarily. It is only logical that combat reports are sent on a daily basis by the brigade to the superior command and this very principle implies that combat reports were written on a daily basis. However, I neither signed them nor were they shown to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you write here about events described in combat reports, but you don't know what was in the combat reports; is that what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No further questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any redirect, Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With your leave, Your Honour, I would like to clarify two points that have arisen from the cross-examination by Mr. Waespi. Re-examined by Mr. Stojanovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Vukotic, you said a moment ago in response to the question whether you had seen those buses that at one point you saw a column of military vehicles that arrived at the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then you said that as far as you remember it was in the afternoon of the 14th of July.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, to the best of my recollection, it was in the afternoon of the 14th of July. The day when I talked to Semso Muminovic. I can't recall exactly any more. Was it on the 14th?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We have a series of historical documents, I would call them, that seem to indicate that it was on the 15th. Are you sure that it was on the 14th?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not sure. It could have been on the 14th or the 15th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us try to find out which. I will show you once again one intercept from Dekici, Prosecution Exhibit P121.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And with your leave, Your Honour, only to show that this is an indisputable fact - no, thank you, we won't need the document; it's only about one sentence - ERN page 008485997, a conversation took place between Vuk and Lovac at 1330 hours. Lovac said: "I heard from Semso and discontinued operations."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could this intercept refresh your memory as to the arrival of this column on the 15th?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Well, I don't see how that arises of my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: It does, the date on which day that column arrived. Witness, you may answer that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can be wrong after all this time about the date and hour; however, the military column returned on the day when I had my negotiations with Semso Muminovic. And another thing, very important to stress: Military columns and military units cannot be considered as a static category. The picture I have in my mind of the vehicles returning does not mean that I can notice a column of the brigade from a distance of 3 to 4 hundred metres. I know that I recognised the trucks from the Podrinje detachment of the Special Forces. At that moment, I saw those vehicles and I knew that they belonged to the Zvornik Brigade. Whether the entire Zvornik Brigade returned at that moment, I cannot really say, because I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. I hope that there will be no dispute between us and the Office of the Prosecutor as to when this column of Vinko Pandurevic and the Zvornik Brigade returned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Stojanovic, I believe that was conducted in private session. Shall we go back to the private session?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, for the sake of caution -- although I didn't intend to mention the name but -- the name of the protected witness. But out of an abundance of caution, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll go to the private session, please, and we'll have that place redacted. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Mr. Vukotic, whom you were subordinated to during the critical period?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to establishment, when I was appointed Assistant Chief of Staff for Intelligence as of November 1994, I was subordinated to the Chief of Staff, Mr. Obrenovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: What about the intelligence and security chain of command? In the framework of this chain of command, I mean security and intelligence chain of command, to whom you were subordinated to?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was as Assistant Chief of Staff in disciplinary terms and in every other way responsible to the Chief of Staff; however, it was my duty to send on intelligence reports with which I always familiarised the Chief of Staff to the intelligence department of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: And the intelligence department of the Drina Corps could order you to do something or not to do something.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a rule, yes, they could assign certain tasks to me. But they would have to ask for the approval of the brigade Chief of Staff and he would have to know about it. They could give me certain tasks to carry out in my field of activity; however, this never happened to me in practice. My only oral contact with this department throughout my career in this domain occurred only when it was necessary to gather intelligence or -- which was sensitive or used a sensitive source, which I was not competent to recruit on my own initiative.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any questions out of Judge's question? Yes. Yes, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour, no questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Just one question. Further cross-examination by Mr. Karnavas:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You being part of the intelligence organ, you were not involved in any counter-intelligence activity.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That would be the security organ; correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO VUKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, at this stage, are there any documents to tender, Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, several documents, D128/3, this is the map of Zvornik which we used during the examination-in-chief of the witness; D129/3, the statement of witness Nedzad Ahmetovic made to the investigators on the 28th of September, 2001; and D130/3, the intelligence report signed by Dusko Vukotic of the 18th of July, 1995, delivered to the command of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Any objections, Mr. Waespi?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. President, could we go into private session for one second?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll go to the private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So, Mr. Waespi, concerning with the other two documents, there's no objections from the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, and we also don't have any documents to tender.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. These two documents, D128/3 and D130/3 are admitted into evidence. It is so decided. Well, Witness, thank you very much indeed for coming to The Hague to give your testimony. We all wish you a pleasant journey back home. The usher will show you out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Stojanovic, I understand that the next witness is waiting. At this stage are you going to call the next witness or we'll have a break and continue our proceedings after the break? I'm entirely in your hands.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I would prefer to call the next witness after the break so that we can organise ourselves and be as efficient as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So we'll take a break and we will resume at 12.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please stand up and make the solemn declaration in accordance with the paper Madam Usher is showing to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. You may sit down, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stojanovic. Examined by Mr. Stojanovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, sir. Could you please introduce yourself. What is your first name and your last name?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MARIC
utterances.text: My name is Milan Maric.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For the transcript, could you please spell your name slowly, first your first name and then your last name.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MARIC
utterances.text: Very well. M-i-l-a-n M-a-r-i-c.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Maric. Could you please tell us when and where you were born.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MARIC
utterances.text: I was born on the 21st of October, 1956, in the municipality of Banovici in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you complete your elementary and secondary education?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MARIC
utterances.text: I completed my elementary education in Banovici, and I completed my high school education in Zivinice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is the municipality of Zivinice in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you finished your secondary school, did you continue with your education? When and where?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MARIC
utterances.text: I studied for two years at the Faculty for Electrical Engineering in Tuzla. Then I went to serve my military term. I interrupted my studies. I attended the School for the Reserve Officers in Bileca. After I completed my compulsory military duty, I completed my studies at the Faculty for Political Science in Sarajevo, All People's Defence Department, and I finished these studies in 1986.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter is not sure whether if the witness said 1976 or 1986 when he completed his studies.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say the Faculty of Political Sciences, the Department of All People's Defence, can you explain to us the structure of this. And did you also receive a military education.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MARIC
utterances.text: Faculty had several department, journalism, sociology, political sciences, and there was also a department for All People's Defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I apologise, Mr. Maric. Could you please slow down a little bit so that the interpreters could interpret everything that you are saying. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MARIC
utterances.text: Since I had already served my compulsory military duty, I already had the rank of second lieutenant, and the people who complete that faculty gain that rank, so I already had that rank. Once I completed my studies, I did not get another rank. And later I found a job in that specialty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that during your studies, you acquired certain military knowledge from aspects of military doctrine?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. The concept of the faculty is such that the students, once they have completed that education, acquire certain military knowledge and they leave with the rank of second lieutenant, which is the first officer's rank. All the rules and regulations in the military apply. This is the rank which would be similar to that required to pass the exam of major, but this is the rank of second lieutenant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now we are going back to 1986. After you completed your university education, where did you begin to work?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MARIC
utterances.text: I began to work in the Municipal TO Staff in Banovici as a clerk for operations and training. I did this until 1999. I was the Chief of Security and the Chief for Intelligence and Security Affairs in the Municipal Staff in Banovici. In 1999, I transferred to the district staff in Tuzla as Assistant Chief of the District Staff for Intelligence. I remained there until 1992, when the war broke out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were these professional military duties that you had in the District TO Staff in Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes. I worked as a civilian in the armed forces. That was my status. It was a part of the armed forces. The TO was a part of the armed forces. And this is all that I did from the professional aspect. I would also like to add, all of these duties that I mentioned, besides the regular training for that, I also completed all the required training courses in the training centres of the Yugoslav People's Army, in Pancevo, Sarajevo for intelligence and security affairs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the war broke out in 1992, you were in Tuzla. Where was your family at the time and were you already married then?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes, I'm married. I have two children. I lived with my family in Banovici, and every day I would travel to work to Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Once the war broke out, did you stay in Banovici or did you leave and go somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MARIC
utterances.text: Just before the war broke out - this was on the 9th of May, 1992 - because I was married - my wife comes from Ozren - I sent my family to my wife's parents, and this is where we happened to be when the war broke out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you stay in Ozren, and did you have any military duties in the Army of Republika Srpska in that period?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MARIC
utterances.text: I did work as a regular soldier in Ozren for a period of two months. After that, a brigade unit was formed and I was Assistant for Intelligence Affairs in the brigade until July 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you come to the Zvornik Brigade and what was the reason for your coming to Zvornik in the first place?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MARIC
utterances.text: I came to Zvornik in July, in late July 1993, and the reason for that was as follows: My father was already living in Zvornik. He had some kind of accommodation there. We did not have very good living conditions at Ozren. There were sixteen of us living in one house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you join the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MARIC
utterances.text: This was in late July 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you came to the Zvornik Brigade, can you remember who the commander was of that brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MARIC
utterances.text: The commander of the brigade was Vinko Pandurevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was the Chief of Staff of the Zvornik Brigade at the time and also the deputy commander of the brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MARIC
utterances.text: The Chief of Staff was Dragan Obrenovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you came to the brigade, did you receive your wartime assignment, and where was your first such assignment?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MARIC
utterances.text: Commander Pandurevic gave me seven days' time to adjust, to get to know the units. Then he assigned me to replace the commander of the 4th Battalion because he had a car accident, so I substituted for him for about a month, and then at the end of August or beginning of September I was given the post of commander of the 5th Battalion, which was situated in --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not catch the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Allow me to ask you what your rank was then in 1993. What was your rank?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MARIC
utterances.text: I had the rank of captain. For some time I had had that rank, for about five or six years back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. How long did you stay in this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour, but occasionally the interpretation, as I think us listening in English, know -- are unable to catch some of the things. Perhaps -- and I know Mr. -- they're telling us that in English, and Mr. Stojanovic is obviously not getting that. For example, they didn't get the name of the town that the brigade was in. And perhaps if the case manager would listen to the English, they might be able to help out, because I don't like to interrupt.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Mr. Stojanovic, you could ask a question about the location of the 5th Battalion of the Zvornik Brigade at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you to the Prosecution and Your Honour for your intervention.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Maric, for the purposes of the transcript, you said that you were appointed commander of the 5th Battalion. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was the 5th Battalion located, the 5th Battalion of the Zvornik Brigade? What was the name of the location where it was?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MARIC
utterances.text: The command post of the 5th Battalion was in Staro Selo, that is a hamlet, the hamlet of Staro Selo in Memici. It's on the road Zvornik-Crni Vrh-Memici-Kalesija.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for that clarification. How long did you remain as the commander of the 5th Infantry Battalion?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MARIC
utterances.text: I was at that post for about a year, until September 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened after that? How did your professional career proceed?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MARIC
utterances.text: After that, I became the clerk in the operations sector of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was the chief of the operations sector in the Zvornik Brigade command?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MARIC
utterances.text: The chief of the operations sector was Captain Miodrag Dragutinovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you spend a long time at that post? How long were you at that post?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MARIC
utterances.text: I was at that post until practically the end of October 1995, and from there I took up a new post, Assistant for Operations Affairs in the Manoeuvring Brigade of the Drina Corps, which was headquartered in Kozluk.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did I understand you correctly? Are we talking about October 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MARIC
